\label{lesson:UR-C77-hamesha}



\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ہمیشہ}}

\textbf{\ur{ہمیشہ}} (\emph{hameshā}) is a loan, usually traced to Persian \emph{hamēsha}, \textquotedblleft{}always\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پہلے} (pehle)}{پہلے (pehle)}]{\ur{پہلے} (pehle) — before, first}

\label{lesson:UR-C77-pehle}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for quickly; early, then the Urdu for a delay; late.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پہلے}}
\textbf{\ur{پہلے}} — \emph{pehle} — \textquotedblleft{}before, first\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پہلے}} (\emph{pehle}) is the adverb form of \emph{pahlā}, \textquotedblleft{}first\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL lists \emph{pahlā} under \emph{*prathilla}, a variant of a reconstructed \emph{*prathila}, \textquotedblleft{}first\textquotedblright{}, built on Sanskrit \emph{prathama}, \textquotedblleft{}first\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8652).
\end{cousinweb}
